paragraphs: E.J. Ward sells automated fuel management systems to fleet operators. One platform covers fuel access, real-time monitoring, tank management, telematics, EV charging and reporting.

Access to the pump is controlled and every transaction accounted for, with reports meant to reveal anomalies. Storage tanks are watched from the same software that runs the fuel islands. Warnings for low levels and alarms for leaks or moisture can go out by text and email. EV chargers can be added to an existing installation as a fleet electrifies. There is also a fleet card for fuel and non-fuel transactions.

The about page dates the company to 1974. Its founder built the first fuel management system at the request of the City of San Antonio. The company describes itself as still family-owned and managed. In 2025 it announced a change of ownership and an investment partnership with TPA Investment Partners LLC. Public buyers are pointed to a Sourcewell awarded contract.
